parts.text: In this experiment, you will investigate how the resistance of a filament lamp changes as the potential difference (p.d.) across it changes. The circuit has been set up for you. Carry out the following instructions, referring to Fig. 1.1. Fig. 1.1

parts.label: a
parts.text: (a) • Close the switch. • Adjust the position of the crocodile clip, so that the length l of the slide wire connected is 20.0 cm. • Record in Table 1.1 the value of the p.d. V and the current I for the lamp. • Move the crocodile clip and record values of V and I for l = 40.0 cm, 60.0 cm, 80.0 cm and 100.0 cm. • Open the switch. [2] Table 1.1 l / cm V / V I / A R / Ω 20.0 40.0 60.0 80.0 100.0

ms.label: 1(a)
ms.text:
V all < 4.00 V and to 1dp at least
I all < 1.00 A and to 2dp at least

parts.label: b
parts.text: (b) Calculate, and record in Table 1.1, the resistance R of the lamp at each value of l . Use the equation R = V I . [1]

parts.label: c
parts.text: (c) Plot a graph of R / Ω ( y -axis) against V / V ( x -axis). [4]

ms.label: 1(c)
ms.text:
graph:
axes labelled correct orientation, with quantity and unit
appropriate scales (plots occupying at least ½ grid)
plots all correct to less than ½ small square and precise plots
well-judged line and thin line

ms.label: 1(d)
ms.text:
resistance increases as temperature increases
(R increases with l), brighter lamp = higher (filament) temperature

parts.label: e
parts.text: (e) In this type of experiment, it is possible to change the current and potential difference for the lamp by using a variable resistor instead of a slide wire. On Fig. 1.2, complete the circuit diagram to show a variable resistor used for this purpose. Fig. 1.2 [2]

ms.label: 1(e)
ms.text:

in series and rest of circuit correct
